messages.content: What did Abraham Lincoln say about the telephone?

response.text:
This is a fascinating question that gets at a bit of historical myth! **Abraham Lincoln did *not* actually say anything about the telephone.**

Here's why:

* **Lincoln died in 1865.**
* **Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone in 1876.** 
* **The first successful telephone call was made in 1876.**

Therefore, Lincoln couldn't have possibly commented on the telephone.

**However, there's a persistent (and false) quote attributed to him that circulates online.** It usually goes something like this:

*"Now I can talk to my generals without having to send a messenger."*

This quote is **completely fabricated**. It likely originated as a humorous thought experiment or a modern attempt to imagine Lincoln's reaction to the technology. It's been spread widely, especially on social media, leading many to believe it's a genuine quote.

**In conclusion: There is no historical record of Abraham Lincoln ever speaking about the telephone. Any quote claiming otherwise is a fabrication.**



You can find more information debunking this myth here:

*   **Snopes:** [https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/lincoln-telephone/](https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/lincoln-telephone/)
*   **History.com:** [https://www.history.com/news/abraham-lincoln-telephone-quote-fake](https://www.history.com/news/abraham-lincoln-telephone-quote-fake)
